findings.title: User check only runs when an Integration row already exists
findings.body: The authenticated-user comparison sits after the `Integration.DoesNotExist: return pipeline.next_step()` early return (line 481-482). On a first-time install, where no Integration row exists yet, the check is skipped. A victim can then be tricked into completing OAuth and the pipeline links an installation_id that someone else installed. The validation described in the PR therefore does not cover the main case.

findings.title: Unguarded access to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]
findings.body: `build_integration` only sets `metadata["sender"]` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy. Integrations created before this change, or without a sender from the webhook, have no `sender` key. This line then raises KeyError (or TypeError if sender is not a dict) and returns a 500 instead of the error page. Use `.get` and fail gracefully.

findings.title: Network calls are unguarded and the OAuth request is not validated
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` is outside the try block, so connection errors or timeouts propagate as a 500. `get_user_info` is also unguarded and may raise on a bad token. The request is a POST with an unchecked status, and the `code` may be None. Wrap these calls and route failures to `error()`.

findings.title: Non-constant-time state comparison and unencoded redirect URL
findings.body: The state is compared with `!=` rather than a constant-time comparison. The authorize URL at line 408 is built by f-string without URL-encoding redirect_uri. The test expects the raw, unencoded redirect_uri in the query, so the URL is fragile.

findings.title: Brittle index into responses.calls
findings.body: `responses.calls[2]` depends on the exact number and order of HTTP calls made by the new OAuth step. It will break if any call is added or removed. In addition, the user-mismatch test never exercises the case where no Integration exists yet, which is the unprotected path.
